title: The Photograph That Ate Its Own Address

features.name: the-consumed-foundation
features.desc-on-touch: Where the photograph was taken from, the ground beneath the frame. The image ate it. All that remains is the remembering that something stood here, and the photo's hunger.

features.name: the-address-that-learned-to-fade
features.desc-on-touch: Street number, suburb, postcode—the photograph has begun to erase the place it documents. The address exists only in the caption now, and the caption is forgetting itself.

features.name: the-frame-that-feeds
features.desc-on-touch: The photograph's border is becoming a mouth. Each time someone looks at it, the place in the image recedes slightly further, leaving only the frame and its appetite.

features.name: the-date-that-outlasted-the-place
features.desc-on-touch: 1987 is still written in the margin. The year remains. The location does not. You understand now what photographs can become when they're kept too carefully.

features.name: rows-of-what-once-surrounded
features.desc-on-touch: The orchard rows are fences now—all that delimited the place. The photograph has made the boundaries permanent and eaten everything between them.

inscription: the photograph learned that places owe it their existence; now it collects the debt by forgetting where it was taken

reverie.title: REVERIE — the red earth where the frame learned hunger
narr: She knelt in the red dirt, framing the shot—
the old tree, the homestead dissolving behind it.
You watched from outside the frame. Already,
her eye was teaching the photograph to remember
differently. The place in the viewfinder was becoming
more real than the place beneath your feet.
